errors_A: Claims the `workspace` policy commands refuse with UNSUPPORTED_WORKSPACE_SHAPE on a folder workspace. Binary: `workspace allow-create`, `allow-delete`, `set-mutations` and `show` all succeed on the filesystem-mem workspace; only `workspace dump` and `grant-cross-link` (which go through setup::full_engine) refuse.
Groups fetch/pull/push under the same refusal; they refuse, but with INVALID_INPUT ('mem is not git-backed'), not UNSUPPORTED_WORKSPACE_SHAPE (transport.rs folder_refusal).
Says the mem-repo has 'no working tree'. mem_repo.rs run_init materialises a working tree with README.md on `main`; only the entity branches are never checked out.

Offers `memstead export --format markdown` as the credible path out of the folder shape. Binary on a filesystem-mem workspace: INVALID_INPUT '--format markdown is not yet supported on filesystem-mem'. The `.mem` archive route installs only as a read-only mount.

Presents export-and-reinit as the switching path and says it could not verify a converter, missing that `memstead mem-repo init .` in the existing folder workspace root upgrades it in place: verified with the binary, the folder mem stays mounted with its entities, git-branch mems can be added beside it, and batch-create then succeeds against the folder mem. The engine's own `mem init` refusal says 'Use `memstead mem-repo init` first to migrate'.
errors_B: `memstead quickstart --repo.` is malformed; the flag is `--repo .` (quickstart --help).

'A README.md beside the entities is tolerated' holds only for the loader (entity/source.rs skips README.md). `init` and `quickstart` both refuse a pre-existing README.md in the mem folder with TARGET_NOT_EMPTY (quickstart.rs blocking_entries: every `.md` blocks, README.md included).

The OUTER_REPO_NOT_IGNORING_MEM_REPO health warning fires only when the workspace is nested inside the repo (workspace_root.rs walks from the parent); with the workspace root as the repo root it does not fire. Verified with the binary; a nuance rather than a contradiction.

The --reattach path additionally needs a `[[mem_management.create]]` allowlist rule; without one `mem init` refuses MEM_PATH_NOT_ALLOWED before reaching reattach. With the rule, reattach works as described (verified).
rationale: Both pick the folder shape for the right reasons and correctly name batch-*/recover refusing with UNSUPPORTED_WORKSPACE_SHAPE, the JSONL ledger, timestamp cursors and the gitignore guard. A adds a false claim (workspace policy commands refuse; most work), a wrong export route, and misses the real switching path. B's account of switching (in-place `mem-repo init` keeps workspace.toml, folder mem stays mounted, later mems get branches, `--reattach` for an existing folder mem) is what the binary actually does, and B hedged exactly what it had not run. B also surfaces the one gain that matters for in-repo review: git merge conflicts are a supported, resolvable case. B's errors are a typo and nuances.
